_comment: Fragment 53 — D-99: phase model corrected (Phase 1 closes last), M-POC requirements and Fn_Spec written. Merged 2026-08-22.

nodes.label: D-99 — Phase 1 Opens First and Closes Last
nodes.description: The orchestration phase cannot close until all specs are written and the other two lanes have completed their tasks and the gaps those specs surfaced. Orchestration is finished when the specs have survived execution, not when they are written.
nodes.rationale: A governance phase that closes before its governance has been executed against has proven nothing. Phase 1 is an envelope rather than a segment.

nodes.label: Lane A Loosened the Wrong Rule
nodes.description: The deadlock lived in the phase-start rule, which required a phase to wait for its predecessor's closure. Lane A instead narrowed the phase-close condition to escape it, and the Judge rejected the escape. A phase now opens when the specs its lane needs are accepted.
nodes.rationale: Loosening the close condition made the model weaker in exactly the place it needed to stay strict. The earlier rescoping is retained as the record of a wrong turn rather than deleted.

nodes.label: C-20 Must Enforce a Cycle, Not Strict Serialization
nodes.description: Lane A writes specs, the Judge accepts, the other lanes execute, gaps return through the handoff channel, Lane A corrects, and the orchestration phase closes when the cycle is quiet. A check must verify a lane had an accepted spec boundary before its first commit and that no gap against its specs is still open at closure.
nodes.rationale: Most of the machinery already exists in the phase register and the handoff status field. What is missing is the acceptance record, so the check blocks on the Judge recording a first acceptance rather than on Lane A writing code.

nodes.label: M-POC Requirements — the Anchor an Fn_Spec Needs
nodes.description: The module requirements tier for the professional evidence review lane. It supplies the feature group that the index row could only point at, with its own identifier namespace so no MVP identifier is reused, moved or renumbered.
nodes.rationale: The module was chartered as a portfolio-level business-continuity measure rather than a product feature, which is the whole of its authority and why it is not a monetization violation. Payment is an operating activity performed outside the application.

nodes.label: The Sharpest Constraint — the Article Stays Internal
nodes.description: Every engagement produces two folders under one identifier. The client package carries explainable content and the evidence ledger; the publishable article stays in the internal folder and must not be copied, linked, embedded or exported into the client-facing one.
nodes.rationale: A spec that satisfies every other requirement and leaks the article has failed the module. The client pays for evidence review and receives explainable content; the publishable article is the MVP's output.

nodes.label: FN-POC-ENGAGEMENT — Behaviour Only, and It Stops There
nodes.description: The functional specification for an engagement: trigger resolution to a URL at the unchanged intake, traversal of the unchanged gates, a named human publish decision, and two separated folders. Its technical-candidate list is deliberately empty.
nodes.rationale: The three input sections cannot function without each other, which is what makes them a feature group rather than three specs restating one another. The spec stops at the tier the Judge authorized, and the next tier is blocked by a decision rather than by an omission.

nodes.label: Hold and Escalate Are Not Respecified
nodes.description: A held or escalated engagement terminates without publication, and its downstream handling is the existing exception behaviour rather than a module-specific variant.
nodes.rationale: A module-specific variant of an existing exception path would be a fork of the pipeline, which the standing invariant forbids and which the module's own invariance requirement exists to prevent.
